summary: Stone fire tower on Owl's Head in Groton State Forest: a 1924 report describes it, trail guides credit CCC work in the 1930s, and it is listed as standing.

facts.design: Octagonal stone tower with a cabin for the fire lookout watchman (1924 report)
facts.agency: Vermont Commissioner of Forestry (per the 1924 report)

access.note: The Owl's Head trail is open within Groton State Forest and is on the state trail finder. We found no source saying the stone tower itself is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: A 2-mile trail, per one trail guide, starts off the Osmore Pond picnic connector road and climbs stone stairs and ledge to the summit.

events.note: First mention in our sources: a 1924 forestry report describes a road to a parking area below the summit, an octagonal stone tower and a cabin for the fire lookout watchman

notes_for_editor: Construction date is unresolved. The 1924 Commissioner of Forestry report already describes an octagonal stone tower, while a trail guide and Wikipedia credit CCC work in the 1930s. An earlier tower may have been rebuilt by the CCC, but no source we read says so. Wikipedia's park photo caption calls the summit building a 'CCC-built shelter', which may or may not be the tower. Groton State Forest history guide and Living New Deal pages returned HTTP 403 and were not read; a search snippet from Living New Deal gives 1935, unverified. Whether the 2002 NRHP listing of park CCC facilities includes the tower is not confirmed. Status 'standing' rests on the FFLA list alone. Wikipedia gives the summit at 596 m (1,956 ft), which is the mountain's height, not the tower's; the record's elevation_m is null. No staffing or fire history found. Interior and climbing access not found.
